subject.title: fix(mcp): reject mixed command+url transport config (#72111)

question: Should OpenClaw treat simultaneous `command` and `url` as an invalid configuration to reject, or support an explicit managed-local-process-plus-HTTP MCP workflow for the scenario reported in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72111?
rationale: The patch improves an ambiguous failure, but the report’s central workflow uses `command` to launch a local HTTP-serving MCP process and `url` to connect to it; choosing rejection versus supported composition changes the lasting MCP configuration contract.

options.title: Define mixed fields as invalid
options.body: Keep the early rejection, add an upgrade-facing Doctor or documented recovery path, and prove the warning with a real configured MCP server.

options.title: Support managed HTTP launch
options.body: Design an explicit configuration and lifecycle contract that starts the local process, waits for its HTTP endpoint, and connects through the selected HTTP transport.

recommendation.title: Define mixed fields as invalid
recommendation.body: Keep the early rejection, add an upgrade-facing Doctor or documented recovery path, and prove the warning with a real configured MCP server.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the evidenced repository-member participant who requested the branch’s required refresh and can route the MCP contract decision.
